summary_paragraph: A 52-year-old female with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, systemic lupus erythematosus, calciphylaxis, and a history of ventricular tachycardia was admitted for monitored sodium thiosulfate therapy during dialysis due to arrhythmia risk. She presented asymptomatic but was found to have a rising lactate up to 9.4 mmol/L. Shortly after arrival, she suffered a pulseless ventricular tachycardia/fibrillation arrest requiring resuscitation, intubation, and ICU admission. She recovered initially and was extubated after 24 hours, receiving sodium thiosulfate with only a brief asymptomatic VT episode. Her course was complicated by septic shock from Klebsiella bacteremia and C. difficile colitis, requiring vasopressors and antibiotics. She developed aspiration pneumonia, acute systolic heart failure with EF dropping to 25%, and recurrent lactic acidosis. Despite stabilization, she deteriorated again with hypotension and altered mental status. After a discussion with her healthcare proxy, her code status was changed to DNR/DNI. She was readmitted to the ICU on pressors and died from pulseless VT on 2166-11-05.
problems: Cardiac arrest due to underlying cardiac condition
